question.leadin: A powerful family that ruled this city included men like Lorezno the Magnificent.
question.text: Name this Italian city once ruled by the Medici family. This city is the most populous one in Tuscany.
question.clue: After Turin and before Rome became capital, it was the capital of the Kingdom of Italy.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about weird things generals did in World War II.
swap.text: General George Patton slapped two soldiers during the invasion of this island. Operation Husky was the codename for an Allied invasion of this island in the south of Italy.
swap.clue: A disastrous military campaign in this region was supported by Alcibiades and contributed to Athens's defeat in the Peloponnesian War.

question.leadin: This bearded warrior led the Expedition of the Thousand while conquering the Kingdom of Two Sicilies for King Victor Emmanuel II.
question.text: Name this leader of the Red Shirts during Italian unification.
question.clue: He was ordered not to attack Trentino, but he earlier defeated the Neapolitans at the Volturno River.

swap.text: This prime minister of the Kingdom of Piedmont-Sardinia and founder of the newspaper Il Risorgimento became the first prime minister of the unified Kingdom of Italy.
swap.clue: This politician ceded Nice and Savoy to that other leader in exchange for assistance in a war that included the Battle of Solferino.

question.leadin: This kingdom was ruled by the House of Savoy.
question.text: Name this state that partially existed at the foot of the Alps and partially on an island.
question.clue: This kingdom was granted the Albertine Constitution by a king whose political ambitions were crushed by Joseph Radetzky at the battles of Novara and Custoza.

swap.text: This large Italian banking family active during the Renaissance included Lorenzo the Magnificent and flourished during the life of Cosimo.
swap.clue: The Pazzi Conspiracy failed to kill Giuliano and Lorenzo of this family.

question.leadin: Many city-states in Italy grew very rich and prosperous after the 4th Crusade.
question.text: This city-state became an autonomous Duchy after the 1183 CE Peace of Constance. Today, this city is the capital of Lombardy and is the 2nd most populous Italian city.
question.clue: The assassination of Gian Galeazzo Maria ("jahn gah-lay-AHT-so Maria") allowed a ruler of this city and ally of Charles VIII to consolidate power.

swap.leadin: An artistically inclined member of this family named Galeazzo Maria was murdered in 1476.
swap.text: Name this family whose most famous member was nicknamed "The Moor."
swap.clue: Prominent members included one who was briefly exiled after trying to displace Bona of Savoy; the cardinal Ascanio; and someone who married the daughter of the duke of Ferrara, Beatrice d'Este, in 1491.

question.leadin: The cristallo produced in this city was the first completely transparent form of glass ever manufactured.
question.text: Name this city, whose island of Murano was long a hub for glassmaking.
question.clue: Its first patron saint was Theodore, but in 828 it obtained the relics of Saint Mark.

swap.text: Engineered by Peter III of Aragon, it was ended by the Peace of Caltabellota, which put Frederick III on the throne. For 15 points, name this conflict, begun during the ringing of bells for a liturgical hour, in which Angevin rule of a Mediteranean island ended.
swap.clue: That king attempted to end this conflict by challenging Peter III of Aragon to personal combat with Edward I serving as the judge of the contest.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Enrico Dandolo, a power broker of medieval European politics.
question.text: Dandolo held this elected leadership title with an Old Italian name. Genoa was ruled by one of these people, and in Dandolo's city they ruled from a palace near Saint Mark's Square.
question.clue: The first was Paolo Lucio Anafesto, and the last one, Ludovico Manin, was deposed by Napoleon.

swap.leadin: This republic fought against Venice in the War of Chioggia ("kee-OH-juh").
swap.text: Name this republic, which competed with Venice to dominate the Mediterranean in the 13thand 14thcenturies. Christopher Columbus was born in this republic, whose capital was a city in Liguria.
swap.clue: A territory ruled by this city was attacked in 1553 by a joint Franco-Ottoman force under Turgut Reis.

question.text: The Battle of Legnano took place during the war between the Ghibellines and this rival faction, who had supported the papacy and included such members as Henry the Proud and Henry the Lion.
question.clue: Charles of Anjou helped this group in establishing themselves in their most important city where the Donati and Cerchi families created "black" and "white" factions, Florence.

swap.text: Schola Medica Salernitana's zenith was reached during the reign of these Germanic people. These people name a confederation that defeated Frederick Barbarossa at the Battle of Legnano.
swap.clue: These people, originally known as the Winnili, tricked Odin by having their wives show up at dawn with hair pulled down over their faces.

question.leadin: A map commissioned by a ruler of this name was known as "The Excursion of One Eager to Penetrate the Horizons" and was divided into seven climatic zones.
question.text: Give this name of a king of Sicily, whose father of the same name was the brother of Robert Guiscard ("ro-BEHR ghis-CAR"). That king of this name commissioned a namesake world map, created by Muhammad al-Idrisi at his court in 1138.
question.answerHtml: Roger [or Ruggero ; accept Roger II or (generously) Roger I or Tabula Roger iana or The Map of Roger ]
question.clue: al-Idrisi is best known for a south-up map created for a ruler with this name, whose coronation mantle features two lines and the Islamic date 528. This first King of Sicily's Hauteville Dynasty had this name.

swap.leadin: One of this party's early leaders claimed his approach was influenced by Benedetto Croce.
swap.text: Name this Italian political party founded by Antonio Gramsci and once led by Palmiro Togliatti. It entered a "historic compromise" with its country's Christian Democrats in the 1970s.
swap.clue: This organization joined the CLN on the eve of World War II as part of a strategy known as the Salerno turn.

question.text: After retiring, Cassiodorus founded this monastery on his property in Squillace ("squee-LAH-chay") near the Castellum. While at this monastery, whose name means "fishpond," Cassiodorus wrote the encyclopedic handbook Institutes.

swap.text: This Italian general would have better luck attacking Ethiopia, and himself became Prime Minister after Mussolini was overthrown.
swap.clue: This man, who had led the Italians to victory over the Ethiopians, succeeded Mussolini as head of the Italian government in 1943, in the midst of the allied invasion in Sicily and southern Italy; he quickly switched allegiance, and declared war on Germany in the autumn of 1943.

question.leadin: This man's murder prompted the so-called Aventine Secession, in which the opposition withdrew from the Chamber of Deputies in protest.
question.text: Identify this Italian Socialist who was killed in 1924, prompting a namesake crisis. Three of his assassins were finally sent to prison after World War II.
question.clue: This Italian socialist politician who was kidnapped and repeatedly stabbed with a carpenter's file after he delivered a speech criticising the impact of the Acerbo Law on elections.

swap.leadin: During this period, right-wing extremists founded the "New Order Scholarship Center", which was banned as a fascist group. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this period of political instability, marked by the violence of paramilitary organizations such as the October 22 Group. This period is often said to run from the death of Antionio Annarumma in 1969 through to the Salerno Massacre in 1982.
swap.clue: This period was preceded by a series of violent strikes known as the Hot Autumn.
